 ‘I’d be hunting at the polls’: Jacksonville man accused of threatening to conduct mass shooting on Election Day
 Staff , News4JAX 
 Published:  November 9, 2026 at 3:14 PM Tags:  Jacksonville , Election Day JSO generic (WJXT) JACKSONVILLE, Fla. – A Jacksonville man is behind bars after investigators say he made a series of written threats online, including posts about hunting people at election polls and conducting mass violence.
 Erik Dorr, 44, was arrested Tuesday and faces one count of written threats to conduct a mass shooting or an act of terrorism, a second-degree felony.
 Recommended Videos
 FDLE Special Agent Sean Lawler said Dorr made dozens of posts to the Fox News digital platform between Feb. 12 and Oct. 31. According to investigators, the posts grew increasingly violent over time, including threats referencing judges, transgender individuals, and election poll workers.
 Among the posts cited in the arrest report, Dorr wrote on Oct. 29, 2026: “I’d be hunting at the polls.” Two days later, on Oct. 31, he allegedly posted: “There are thousands of us hunting at polls. The workers know they aren’t getting away with their usual [expletive] without us beating the [expletive] out of them.”
 On Monday, Nov. 2, FDLE agents, along with JSO detectives and deputies, visited Dorr’s home. 
 Dorr acknowledged the posts were tied to his email address and admitted to writing them, the report said. He told investigators he did not intend to hurt anyone and was “venting” about political frustration. He also stated he did not own any weapons, according to the report.
 His next court appearance is scheduled for Nov. 25.
